newsitem.title: UK: Dollar trickles lower in late, quiet Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dollar trickles lower in late, quiet Europe.

text.p: The dollar was tending to trickle lower against the mark in late European trading with the market winding down for the Christmas and New Year holiday season which begins next week.
"We've seen nothing much today," one trader said. "It's very thin and the only orders are from people adjusting book positions. Christmas holidays seem to have started very early this year."
At 1609 GMT the dollar was at 1.5511/17 compared with around 1.5560 at midsession and Thursday's close of 1.5592/5602. Dollar/yen held steady around Thursday's close at 114.12/22.
Despite its drift lower the dollar's bullish undertone remains intact and another strong performance on Wall Street this afternoon helped limit the losses, traders said.
This, Thursday's better-than-expected U.S. trade data and speculation of a rise in U.S. interest rates early next year should help the dollar end the year on a firm note, they added.
There is also vague background speculation that German monetary policy will tend to remain fairly slack after data showing still subdued price pressure.
Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing confirmed the German central bank's ease with price pressure in Germany.
"We are in a phase of stability in the price of money, which is favourable such as never before," Issing said in an interview on Thursday.

On consumer prices, the states of Hesse and Bavaria reported an expected 0.3 percent rise in consumer prices in December while Baden Wuerttemberg CPI was up just 0.2 percent. Analysts said this points to an unchanged annual rate of 1.4 percent.
U.S. data today had little or no impact with U.S. Q3 GDP revised to 2.1 percent growth against a provisional 2.0 percent with final sales up 0.5 percent and the GDP price index up 2.0.
The mark itself was little changed on the crosses with mark/lira steady at 983.95/4.45 compared with Thursday's close of 982.80/3.00.
There is some speculation that Italy will cut rates after the market closes today against the background of benign inflation data.
